# The pinned CI tools, one row per tool - read by ./install.sh (which installs
# one) and by ../../scripts/check_tool_versions.sh (which reports drift against
# each upstream's latest release). Both reach it through ./lib.sh, so this file
# is the single roster: a tool pinned here cannot go undrift-checked.
#
#   name|pin|kind|url|verify|check|tag-prefix
#
# name    the first column an `uses: ./.github/actions/setup-tool` names, and
#         the executable's name - install.sh saves a `raw` download under it,
#         and finds it inside an archive with `find -name <name>`.
# pin     the version, WITHOUT a leading "v" even where upstream's tag has one:
#         some projects tag v1.2.3 but name the asset 1.2.3, and only one
#         placeholder is substituted. The url column carries the literal "v"
#         (or, for lychee, "lychee-v") where the tag needs it.
# kind    raw (a bare executable) or tar.gz (an archive to search inside).
#         cmake/make kinds could be added here for a tool that ships only as
#         source, if one is ever needed.
# url     %v is the pin. %a would be the asset slug for this runner
#         (linux.x86_64 / darwin.aarch64 / darwin.x86_64), resolved first so a
#         version can never be mistaken for one - unused below because every
#         job that installs one of these runs on Linux.
# verify  the flag install.sh runs the installed tool with as a smoke test.
# check   where to look for the latest release: github:<owner>/<repo>, or "-"
#         to opt out of the drift report entirely.
# tag-prefix  optional 7th column, only needed when upstream's release tag
#         does not look like "v<pin>" - check_tool_versions.sh strips this
#         (default "v") off the upstream tag before comparing to `pin`, which
#         never carries a prefix of its own. Blank for every row except
#         lychee, whose tags read "lychee-v<version>".
# sha256  8th column: the expected sha256 of the downloaded file (the raw
#         binary, or the tar.gz archive before it's extracted) at this exact
#         pin. install.sh verifies it after download and refuses to install a
#         mismatch, so a compromised release asset or a MITM'd download is
#         rejected instead of silently landing on PATH and running as part of
#         CI. Computed once, when the pin is set, with
#         `curl -sSL <url> | sha256sum` (substitute the real %v/%a first) -
#         this is *not* re-fetched from upstream on every run, so it changes
#         only in the same commit that bumps `pin`, and a bumped pin with an
#         unchanged sha256 is itself a red flag worth double-checking by hand.
#
# Bumping a pin is a hand edit here, and nothing else - the caching action.yml
# reads the version back out of install.sh's `resolve`.
zizmor|1.30.0|tar.gz|https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/releases/download/v%v/zizmor-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz|--version|github:zizmorcore/zizmor||ec8c95cd800845abb9bbc5f377ec7c57d2eb8e2386a00a201d3a74ee4092e5ed
actionlint|1.7.12|tar.gz|https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/releases/download/v%v/actionlint_%v_linux_amd64.tar.gz|--version|github:rhysd/actionlint||8aca8db96f1b94770f1b0d72b6dddcb1ebb8123cb3712530b08cc387b349a3d8
# verify is "llvm-cov --version", not the bare flag every other row uses: the
# binary is a cargo subcommand plugin - built the same way "cargo llvm-cov ..."
# works, by expecting its own subcommand name as the first argument even when
# invoked directly (cargo does that prepending itself when it dispatches to
# it; this smoke test has to do it by hand). A bare "cargo-llvm-cov --version"
# fails with "expected subcommand 'llvm-cov', found argument '--version'".
# Downstream usage in coverage.yml is unaffected either way: it always goes through
# `cargo llvm-cov ...`, which cargo itself resolves the same correct way.
cargo-llvm-cov|0.9.0|tar.gz|https://github.com/taiki-e/cargo-llvm-cov/releases/download/v%v/cargo-llvm-cov-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz|llvm-cov --version|github:taiki-e/cargo-llvm-cov||b068f7c98841aacb9c4f382b4a0c184ae82f49b56a32d442b429b2961c73be15
# lychee tags its releases "lychee-v<version>", not "v<version>" like every
# other row here - the url column copes fine (the literal "lychee-v" prefix
# just sits in front of %v). The trailing "lychee-v" column is what lets
# check_tool_versions.sh compare correctly instead of misreading
# "lychee-v0.24.2" as newer than any pin forever, which is why this row no
# longer needs `check = "-"` to opt out of drift checking entirely.
lychee|0.24.2|tar.gz|https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee/releases/download/lychee-v%v/lychee-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz|--version|github:lycheeverse/lychee|lychee-v|1f4e0ef7f6554a6ed33dd7ac144fb2e1bbed98598e7af973042fc5cd43951c9a
typos|1.50.1|tar.gz|https://github.com/crate-ci/typos/releases/download/v%v/typos-v%v-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz|--version|github:crate-ci/typos||edf0545109aee6a22751d04ddecb97c45be47d3aa0409564fb895eeeace91b1e
